/-- The leaf `dst` of a usable place belongs to its own footprint (§40; support for DS-v2). -/
theorem mem_footprint_self {s : S3} {d : Nat} (hu : s.Usable d) (hl : isLeaf s.P d) :
    d ∈ footprint s.P d :=
  mem_footprint.2 ⟨hu.lt, hl, hu.lt, .inl rfl⟩

/-! ## `rewind` (DS-v2) -/

/-- `rewind_rejects_live_above` (DS-v2, non-normative: "rewind m … rejects if an active authority
derived from internal covers a cell above m"): for a live mark `m` of an existing stack (its stack
live, DS2-3), if an active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m` (at a position
`≥ m.top`, DS2-4), `rewind m`
has the outcome `reject` and no other: either the administrative right of §36 fails, or `split` of
`internal` on the cells above `m` is rejected, since `internal` no longer has effective `Modify` on
that cell (§43, §61.1). -/
theorem rewind_rejects_live_above {k : K} {D : DState} {j : Nat} {st : Stack} {m : Mark}
    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (hm : LiveMark D.kern j st m) {x l : Nat} {y : Authority}
    (hy : D.kern.A[x]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true) (hx : st.internal ∈ D.kern.ancs x)
    (hly : l ∈ y.footprint) (hl : l ∈ above st m) :
    RewindStep k j m D .reject ∧ ∀ o, RewindStep k j m D o → o = .reject := by
  have hn : ¬ SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [above st m] := fun h =>
    no_desc_of_modify hy ya hly hx (h.modifyOn _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl)
  refine ⟨?_, fun o ho => ?_⟩
  · by_cases ha : AdminRight D.kern st
    · exact .split hst hm ha (.reject hn)
    · exact .static hst hm ha
  · cases ho with
    | noStack h => rw [hst] at h; cases h
    | dead h hd => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd hm hd
    | static => rfl
    | split => rfl
    | release => rfl
    | ok h _ _ hsp =>
      rw [hst] at h; cases h
      exact absurd (Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp).1 hn

/-- `rewind_keeps_older_marks` (DS-v2, non-normative: "otherwise returns those cells to available
and removes m and every mark above it"; §46 metadata, §62 `ok` effect): after an `ok` of
`rewind m`, the marks of the stack are exactly those older than `m`, its top is the top of `m`
(the cells above `m` are available again), the other stacks are unchanged, and no initialization
changes. -/
theorem rewind_keeps_older_marks {k : K} {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark}
    (h : RewindStep k j m D (.ok D')) {st : Stack} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st)
    {pre post : List Mark} (hs : st.marks = pre ++ m :: post) (hpre : m ∉ pre) :
    (∃ st', D'.stacks[j]? = some st' ∧ st'.marks = pre ∧ st'.top = m.top) ∧
      (∀ i, i ≠ j → D'.stacks[i]? = D.stacks[i]?) ∧ D'.kern.I = D.kern.I := by
  cases h with
  | ok hst₀ _ _ hsp hrl =>
    rw [hst] at hst₀; cases hst₀
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hrl
    refine ⟨⟨_, List.getElem?_set_self (lt_of_getElem? hst), ?_, rfl⟩,
      fun i hi => List.getElem?_set_ne (Ne.symm hi), ?_⟩
    · simp only [rewindMeta]; rw [hs]; exact takeWhile_ne_append post hpre
    · rw [releaseEff_I]; rfl

/-! ## When `rewind` is `ok` (DS-v2) -/

/-- Anchors name existing authorities (support for DS-v2, non-normative, `rewind`; §44: `D(q)`
holds authority identities; §42: identities index `A`): every anchor of every place is an index of
`A`. -/
....
theorem DReach.blocksHeld {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (h : DReach k statics D) :
    BlocksHeld D := by
  induction h with
  | init => intro i st h; simp [DState.init] at h
  | step _ hs ih => exact hs.blocksHeld ih

/-- On library-reachable states a place holds the authority of every block of a stack, so `grow`
always has a destination and `GrowStep.noHolder` never applies there (DS-v2, non-normative, DS2-2;
§42, §65). -/
theorem DReach.grow_holder {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (h : DReach k statics D)
    {j b : Nat} {st : Stack} {x : Blk} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (hx : st.block b = some x) :
    ∃ d, holderPlace D.kern b = some d := by
  have hxb : x.auth = b := by simpa using List.find?_some hx
  obtain ⟨y, hy, hp⟩ := h.blocksHeld j st hst x (List.mem_of_find?_eq_some hx)
  rw [hxb] at hy
  unfold holderPlace; rw [hy]
  cases hh : y.holder with
  | place v => exact ⟨v, by simp [hh]⟩
  | frame f => rw [hh] at hp; cases hp

/-- The authority added by `split` of `src` on one region can be released at once (support for
DS-v2, non-normative, `rewind`; §62): it is active, derived, held by the current frame (§62.1,
§62.2), has no descendant (§62.3: origins precede, §42) and, under `DBound`, anchors no place
(§62.3, §62.4). -/
theorem release_after_split {s : S3} {src : Nat} {R : List Nat} (hb : DBound s) :
    ReleasePre (splitEff s src [R]) s.A.length := by
  have hy₀ := split_block s src R
  refine ⟨⟨_, hy₀, rfl⟩, by rw [hy₀]; simp [OptP], by rw [hy₀]; exact rfl,
    fun j hj hn => ?_, fun q _ _ hx => absurd (hb q _ hx) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)⟩
  have := chain_lt hn
  have := List.mem_range.1 hj; simp [splitEff] at this; omega

/-- `rewind_ok_iff` (DS-v2, non-normative: "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an
active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to
available"; §36; §61.1, §61.3, §62 through Part XIV). On a library-reachable state (`DReach`, a
state invariant), for an existing stack, `rewind m` is `ok` exactly when `m` is a live mark of the
stack (DS-v2: its stack is live, DS2-3), the administrative right of §36 holds (`AdminRight`,
DS-v2, Q27 (a)), and no active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m` (DS-v2;
DS2-4: a cell at a position `≥ m.top`).
The model has no explicit check of the last condition: it is the effective `Modify` of `internal`
required by `split` (§61.1, with the effective mode of §43). The other checks of `split` and
`release` never reject there: `internal` has own mode `Modify` and covers the cells
(`DReach.stackShape`, §76.2, §76.3), and anchors name existing authorities
(`dBound_of_reachable`). With `RewindStep.det`, `ok` is then the only outcome. -/
theorem rewind_ok_iff {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (hr : DReach k statics D)
    {j : Nat} {st : Stack} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) {m : Mark} :
    (∃ D', RewindStep k j m D (.ok D')) ↔
      LiveMark D.kern j st m ∧ AdminRight D.kern st ∧
        ∀ (x l : Nat) (y : Authority), D.kern.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
          st.internal ∈ D.kern.ancs x → l ∈ y.footprint → l ∉ above st m := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨D', h⟩
    cases h with
    | ok h hm ha hsp =>
      rw [hst] at h; cases h
      have hp := (Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp).1
      exact ⟨hm, ha, fun x l y hy ya hx hly hl =>
        no_desc_of_modify hy ya hly hx (hp.modifyOn _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hm, ha, hno⟩
    obtain ⟨yi, hyi, hmi, hci⟩ := hr.stackShape j st hst
    have yia : yi.active = true := by
      obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := ha.1; rw [hyi] at hy; cases hy; exact ya
    have hab : ∀ l ∈ above st m, l ∈ yi.footprint := fun l hl => hci l (List.mem_of_mem_drop hl)
    have hmod : ∀ l ∈ above st m, effective D.kern st.internal l = some .modify := by
      intro l hl
      have hd : descModes D.kern st.internal l = [] := by
        apply nil_of_forall_not_mem; intro e he
        obtain ⟨x, y, hy, ya, hly, hx, -⟩ := mem_descModes.1 he
        exact hno x l y hy ya hx hly hl
      rw [effective_eq hyi yia (hab l hl), hd]; simp [effOf, hmi]
    have hex : D.kern.ExercisableAt st.internal .modify := by
      have hmr := ha.2
      simp only [MetaRight, arenaValue, Stack.entry, hyi] at hmr
      cases hv : yi.holder with
      | frame f => rw [hv] at hmr; exact hmr.elim
      | place v =>
        rw [hv] at hmr
        obtain ⟨b, -, hb, hall⟩ := hmr
        exact .held hyi yia (.inr hmi) hv hb hall
    have hsp : SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [above st m] := by
      refine ⟨ha.1, hex, fun r hr p hp => ?_, fun r hr p hp => ?_, List.pairwise_singleton _ _,
        fun r hr p hp x _ hd => ?_⟩
      · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr] at hp; exact hmod p hp
      · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr] at hp
        exact ⟨by simp only [S3.afp, hyi]; exact hab p hp, by rw [hmod p hp]; simp⟩
      · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr] at hp
        unfold DistribExcl at hd
        cases hx : D.kern.A[x]? with
        | none => rw [hx] at hd; exact hd
        | some y =>
          rw [hx] at hd; obtain ⟨ya, hanc, hpy, -⟩ := hd; exact hno x p y hx ya hanc hpy hp
    exact ⟨_, .ok hst hm ha (.ok hsp)
      (.ok (release_after_split (dBound_of_reachable hr.reachable)))⟩

/-! ## Marks are never reused (`mark_no_aba`) -/

/-- Well-formed marks (DS-v2, non-normative, "marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark
identifier"; support; library metadata, §38): the live marks of stack `i` are pairwise distinct,
name stack `i`, and have identifiers already given out. -/
def MarksWF (D : DState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), D.stacks[i]? = some st →
    st.marks.Nodup ∧ ∀ m ∈ st.marks, m.stack = i ∧ m.id < D.fresh

/-- A removed mark (DS-v2, non-normative; support; library metadata, §38): its identifier was
given out and it is live in no stack. -/
def Gone (D : DState) (m : Mark) : Prop :=
  m.id < D.fresh ∧ ∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), D.stacks[i]? = some st → m ∉ st.marks

/-- The initial state has well-formed marks (DS-v2, §47). -/
theorem marksWF_init (statics : Statics) : MarksWF (DState.init statics) := fun i st h => by
  simp [DState.init] at h

/-- Replacing stack `j` by a stack whose marks are a sublist keeps `MarksWF` when no identifier is
taken back (DS-v2; §38 library metadata). -/
theorem marksWF_set {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} {st st' : Stack} (hw : MarksWF D)
    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (hs : D'.stacks = D.stacks.set j st')
    (hsub : st'.marks.Sublist st.marks) (hf : D.fresh ≤ D'.fresh) : MarksWF D' := by
  intro i st'' h
  rw [hs] at h
  rcases getElem?_set_cases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
  · exact ⟨(hw _ st hst).1.sublist hsub, fun m hm => by
      have := (hw _ st hst).2 m (hsub.subset hm); exact ⟨this.1, by omega⟩⟩
  · exact ⟨(hw i st'' h).1, fun m hm => by
      have := (hw i st'' h).2 m hm; exact ⟨this.1, by omega⟩⟩

/-- Replacing stack `j` by a stack whose marks are a sublist keeps a removed mark removed (DS-v2;
§38 library metadata). -/
theorem gone_set {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} {st st' : Stack} {m : Mark} (hg : Gone D m)
    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (hs : D'.stacks = D.stacks.set j st')
    (hsub : ∀ x ∈ st'.marks, x ∈ st.marks) (hf : D.fresh ≤ D'.fresh) : Gone D' m := by
  refine ⟨by have := hg.1; omega, fun i st'' h hm => ?_⟩
  rw [hs] at h
  rcases getElem?_set_cases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
  · exact hg.2 _ st hst (hsub m hm)
  · exact hg.2 i st'' h hm

/-- Every library step keeps `MarksWF` (DS-v2; §38 library metadata). -/
theorem DStep.marksWF {k : K} {D D' : DState} (h : DStep k D D') (hw : MarksWF D) :
    MarksWF D' := by
  cases h with
  | kernel => exact hw
  | newStack hs =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
    intro i st h
    rcases getElem?_append_single h with h | rfl
    · exact hw i st h
    · exact ⟨List.nodup_nil, fun m hm => by simp at hm⟩
  | push hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok hst => exact marksWF_set hw hst rfl (List.Sublist.refl _) (Nat.le_refl _)
  | rewind hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok hst => exact marksWF_set hw hst rfl (List.takeWhile_sublist _) (Nat.le_refl _)
  | grow hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok hst => exact marksWF_set hw hst rfl (List.Sublist.refl _) (Nat.le_refl _)
  | mark hs =>
    cases hs with
    | @ok st hst _ =>
      intro i st' h
      rcases getElem?_set_cases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
      · obtain ⟨hnd, hms⟩ := hw _ st hst
        refine ⟨List.nodup_append.2 ⟨hnd, List.nodup_cons.2 ⟨by simp, List.nodup_nil⟩,
          fun a ha b hb e => ?_⟩, fun m hm => ?_⟩
        · rw [List.mem_singleton] at hb; subst hb; subst e
          exact Nat.lt_irrefl _ (hms _ ha).2
        · rcases List.mem_append.1 hm with hm | hm
          · exact ⟨(hms m hm).1, Nat.lt_succ_of_lt (hms m hm).2⟩
          · rw [List.mem_singleton] at hm; subst hm; exact ⟨rfl, Nat.lt_succ_self _⟩
      · exact ⟨(hw i st' h).1, fun m hm =>
          ⟨((hw i st' h).2 m hm).1, Nat.lt_succ_of_lt ((hw i st' h).2 m hm).2⟩⟩

/-- Every library-reachable state has well-formed marks (DS-v2; §47 initial state). -/
theorem DReach.marksWF {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (h : DReach k statics D) :
    MarksWF D := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact marksWF_init statics
  | step _ hs ih => exact hs.marksWF ih

/-- Every library step keeps a removed mark removed: identifiers are fresh (DS-v2; §38 library
metadata). -/
theorem DStep.gone {k : K} {D D' : DState} {m : Mark} (h : DStep k D D') (hg : Gone D m) :
    Gone D' m := by
  cases h with
  | kernel => exact hg
  | newStack hs =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
    refine ⟨hg.1, fun i st h hm => ?_⟩
    rcases getElem?_append_single h with h | rfl
    · exact hg.2 i st h hm
    · simp at hm
  | push hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact gone_set hg hst rfl (fun _ h => h) (Nat.le_refl _)
  | rewind hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok hst => exact gone_set hg hst rfl (fun _ h => List.takeWhile_subset _ h) (Nat.le_refl _)
  | grow hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact gone_set hg hst rfl (fun _ h => h) (Nat.le_refl _)
  | mark hs =>
    cases hs with
    | @ok st hst _ =>
      refine ⟨Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hg.1, fun i st' h hm => ?_⟩
      rcases getElem?_set_cases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
      · rcases List.mem_append.1 hm with hm | hm
        · exact hg.2 _ st hst hm
        · rw [List.mem_singleton] at hm; rw [hm] at hg; exact Nat.lt_irrefl _ hg.1
      · exact hg.2 i st' h hm

/-- Every run keeps a removed mark removed (DS-v2; §38 library metadata). -/
theorem DRun.gone {k : K} {D D' : DState} {m : Mark} (h : DRun k D D') (hg : Gone D m) :
    Gone D' m := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact hg
  | tail _ hs ih => exact hs.gone ih

/-- `rewind` of a mark that is not live for an existing stack (dead, foreign, or of a dead stack)
fails, with no other outcome, whatever the rights of the current frame (DS-v2, non-normative:
"rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark", checked before the right of §36; §58 `fail`). -/
theorem rewind_dead_fails {k : K} {D : DState} {i : Nat} {st : Stack} {m : Mark}
    (hst : D.stacks[i]? = some st) (hm : ¬ LiveMark D.kern i st m) :
    RewindStep k i m D .fail ∧ ∀ o, RewindStep k i m D o → o = .fail := by
  refine ⟨.dead hst hm, fun o ho => ?_⟩
  cases ho with
  | noStack => rfl
  | dead => rfl
  | static h hl => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd hl hm
  | split h hl => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd hl hm
  | release h hl => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd hl hm
  | ok h hl => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd hl hm

/-- `rewind_dead_stack_fails` (DS-v2, non-normative, DS2-3: a dead stack invalidates its marks;
§46 read for a stack: the stack is live if `internal` is active; §58 `fail`): on an existing stack
whose `internal` is inactive, `rewind m` fails, with no other outcome, for every mark `m` and
whatever the rights of the current frame. -/
theorem rewind_dead_stack_fails {k : K} {D : DState} {j : Nat} {st : Stack} {m : Mark}
    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (hd : ¬ D.kern.Active st.internal) :
    RewindStep k j m D .fail ∧ ∀ o, RewindStep k j m D o → o = .fail :=
  rewind_dead_fails hst fun h => hd h.1

/-- `mark_no_aba` (DS-v2, non-normative: marks carry a fresh identifier; `rewind m` removes `m` and
every mark above it): every mark removed by an `ok` of `rewind m`, `m` and every later mark of the
stack, is live in no stack after any later run, even when the top returns to its position, and its
`rewind` fails, with no other outcome (§58), on every existing stack. Under `MarksWF`, which holds
on every library-reachable state (`DReach.marksWF`). -/
theorem mark_no_aba {k : K} {D D₁ D' : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} (hw : MarksWF D)
    (hr : RewindStep k j m D (.ok D₁)) (hrun : DRun k D₁ D') {st : Stack}
    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) {pre post : List Mark} (hs : st.marks = pre ++ m :: post)
    {m' : Mark} (hm' : m' ∈ m :: post) :
    (∀ (i : Nat) (st' : Stack), D'.stacks[i]? = some st' → m' ∉ st'.marks) ∧
      ∀ (i : Nat) (st' : Stack), D'.stacks[i]? = some st' →
        RewindStep k i m' D' .fail ∧ ∀ o, RewindStep k i m' D' o → o = .fail := by
  obtain ⟨hnd, hms⟩ := hw j st hst
  rw [hs] at hnd
  have hdisj := (List.nodup_append.1 hnd).2.2
  have hmpre : m ∉ pre := fun h => hdisj m h m (List.mem_cons_self ..) rfl
  have hm'st : m' ∈ st.marks := by rw [hs]; exact List.mem_append_right _ hm'
  obtain ⟨⟨st₁, hst₁, hpre₁, -⟩, hother, -⟩ := rewind_keeps_older_marks hr hst hs hmpre
  have hf : D₁.fresh = D.fresh := by cases hr; rfl
  have hg : Gone D₁ m' := by
    refine ⟨by rw [hf]; exact (hms m' hm'st).2, fun i st'' h hin => ?_⟩
    by_cases hij : i = j
    · subst hij; rw [hst₁] at h; cases h; rw [hpre₁] at hin
      exact hdisj m' hin m' hm' rfl
    · rw [hother i hij] at h
      exact hij (((hw i st'' h).2 m' hin).1.symm.trans (hms m' hm'st).1)
  have hg' := hrun.gone hg
  exact ⟨hg'.2, fun i st' h => rewind_dead_fails h fun hl => hg'.2 i st' h hl.2.2⟩

/-! ## `grow` (DS-v2) -/

/-- `grow_same_base` (DS-v2, non-normative: "grow is in place only (same base, extension into the
space directly after the block)"; DS2-2: the new block authority goes to the place that currently
holds `b`; DS2-5: `extra` may be zero): an `ok` of `grow b extra` grows the block of authority `b`
of the stack in place: the extension is in place; the metadata records the grown block of the
same base, `extra` more cells, the new authority and, as destination, the place `d` that held `b`
when `grow` started; in the arrival state that authority, of fresh identity, is an active `Modify`
derived from `internal` covering the cells from the same base and held by `d` (§61, §65 `ok`
effects); the old cells are a prefix of the new ones; `b` is inactive (§62). -/
theorem grow_same_base {k : K} {D D' : DState} {j b extra : Nat}
    (h : GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok D')) :
    ∃ st x d, D.stacks[j]? = some st ∧ st.block b = some x ∧ InPlace st x extra ∧
      holderPlace D.kern b = some d ∧
      D'.stacks[j]? = some (growMeta st x extra D.kern.A.length d) ∧
      growBlk x extra D.kern.A.length d ∈ (growMeta st x extra D.kern.A.length d).blocks ∧
      D'.kern.A[D.kern.A.length]? =
        some ⟨.modify, some st.internal, cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra), .place d, true⟩ ∧
      cellsOf st x.base x.size <+: cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra) ∧
      ¬ D'.kern.Active b := by
  cases h with
  | @ok st x s₁ s₂ s₃ d hst hx hrl hd hstat hin hsp hsto =>
    obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hrl
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsto
    have hlen := releaseEff_len D.kern b
    obtain ⟨yb, hyb, -⟩ := hpre.active
    have hbl : b < D.kern.A.length := lt_of_getElem? hyb
    have hblk := split_block (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra))
    have hnew :=
      issued_block (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal d (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra))
    rw [hlen] at hblk hnew ⊢
    refine ⟨st, x, d, hst, hx, hin, hd, List.getElem?_set_self (lt_of_getElem? hst),
      List.mem_map.2 ⟨x, List.mem_of_find?_eq_some hx, by simp⟩, hnew, cellsOf_prefix st _ _ _, ?_⟩
    rintro ⟨y, hy, ya⟩
    rw [storeEff_eq hblk] at hy
    simp only at hy
    rw [List.getElem?_set_ne (by omega)] at hy
    simp only [splitEff, List.map_cons, List.map_nil] at hy
    rw [List.getElem?_append_left (by rw [hlen]; exact hbl), releaseEff_eq hyb,
      List.getElem?_set_self hbl] at hy
    cases hy; simp at ya

/-- `grow_keeps_prefix_init` (DS-v2, non-normative; §62, §61, §65 `ok` effects): `grow` changes the
initialization of no cell of the old block: `release` and `split` change no initialization, and
`store` initializes only its destination, the place that held `b` (DS2-2), which the new block does
not cover (§65.3). -/
theorem grow_keeps_prefix_init {k : K} {D D' : DState} {j b extra : Nat}
    (h : GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok D')) {st : Stack} {x : Blk} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st)
    (hx : st.block b = some x) : ∀ l ∈ cellsOf st x.base x.size, D'.kern.I l = D.kern.I l := by
  cases h with
  | @ok _ _ _ _ _ d hst₀ hx₀ hrl _ _ _ hsp hsto =>
    rw [hst] at hst₀; cases hst₀; rw [hx] at hx₀; cases hx₀
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hrl
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp
    obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsto
    intro l hl
    have hblk := split_block (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra))
    have hlr : l ∈ (splitEff (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal
        [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)]).afp (releaseEff D.kern b).A.length := by
      simp only [S3.afp, hblk]; exact (cellsOf_prefix st x.base x.size extra).subset hl
    have hne : l ≠ d := fun he =>
      (hpre.noCover l hlr).1 (by rw [he]; exact mem_footprint_self hpre.usable hpre.leaf)
    rw [storeEff_eq hblk]
    simp only [hne, ↓reduceIte]
    show (releaseEff D.kern b).I l = _; rw [releaseEff_I]

/-! ## Bytes of the old block after `grow` (refinement, §82) -/

/-- A raw write into the range of leaf `d` leaves the bytes of the range of a leaf `l` in another
allocation or with a disjoint range unchanged (§16 ¶3, §82.1; support for DS-v2 `grow`). -/
theorem bytesOf_write_other {s2 : Machine.State} {L : Refinement.Layout} {l d : Nat}
    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat}
    (hd : (L l).alloc ≠ (L d).alloc ∨
      Machine.RangeDisjoint (L l).off (L l).len (L d).off (L d).len)
    {i : Nat} (hi : i < (L l).len) :
    Refinement.bytesOf (s2.write (Refinement.leafAcc s2 L .write d) w) L l i =
      Refinement.bytesOf s2 L l i := by
  unfold Refinement.bytesOf
  rw [Refinement.write_allocs]
  by_cases heq : (L l).alloc = (L d).alloc
  · have hr := hd.resolve_left (· heq)
    simp only [Refinement.leafAcc, heq, ↓reduceIte]
    cases ha : s2.allocs (L d).alloc with
    | none => rfl
    | some a =>
      simp only [Option.map_some, Refinement.leafAddr, Refinement.baseOf_of ha,
        Nat.add_sub_cancel_left]
      rw [Machine.Alloc.write_bytes_out]
      intro ⟨h1, h2⟩
      exact hr ((L l).off + i) (Nat.le_add_right _ _) (Nat.add_lt_add_left hi _) h1 h2
  · simp only [Refinement.leafAcc, heq, ↓reduceIte]

/-- `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` (DS-v2, non-normative; through the refinement of Part XVII, §82): an
`ok` of `grow b extra` is the kernel steps `release(b)`, `split(internal, [region])` and
`store(|A|, d)`, `d` the place that held `b` (DS2-2); their realization in the memory machine
(`Refinement.opsOf`) has no raw operation for `release` and `split` (§62, §61), and the raw
operations of `store` (one write into the range of `d`, §82.3) leave the bytes, values and
provenances, of every cell of the old block unchanged, for every layout satisfying the layout
interface `LayoutWF` (§82.1, §23) in the state before the step. -/
theorem grow_keeps_prefix_bytes {Ty : Type} {k : K} {D D' : DState} {j b extra : Nat}
    (h : GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok D')) {st : Stack} {x : Blk} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st)
    (hx : st.block b = some x) :
    ∃ s₁ s₂ d, holderPlace D.kern b = some d ∧ Refinement.OpStep k (.release b) D.kern s₁ ∧
      Refinement.OpStep k (.split st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)]) s₁ s₂ ∧
      Refinement.OpStep k (.store D.kern.A.length d) s₂ D'.kern ∧
      ∀ (π : Refinement.Params Ty) (s2 : Machine.State), Refinement.LayoutWF π.L D.kern s2 →
        Refinement.opsOf π (.release b) D.kern s2 = [] ∧
        Refinement.opsOf π (.split st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)]) s₁ s2 = [] ∧
        ∀ l ∈ cellsOf st x.base x.size, ∀ i < (π.L l).len,
          Refinement.bytesOf
            (Refinement.run s2 (Refinement.opsOf π (.store D.kern.A.length d) s₂ s2)) π.L l i =
          Refinement.bytesOf s2 π.L l i := by
  cases h with
  | @ok st₀ x₀ s₁ s₂ s₃ d hst₀ hx₀ hrl hd hstat hin hsp hsto =>
    rw [hst] at hst₀; cases hst₀; rw [hx] at hx₀; cases hx₀
    have hlen : s₁.A.length = D.kern.A.length := by
      rw [(Guarded.ok_iff.1 hrl).2]; exact releaseEff_len D.kern b
    have hP₁ : s₁.P = D.kern.P := by rw [(Guarded.ok_iff.1 hrl).2]; exact releaseEff_P D.kern b
    have hP₂ : s₂.P = D.kern.P := by rw [(Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp).2, ← hP₁]; rfl
    rw [hlen] at hsto
    refine ⟨s₁, s₂, d, hd, hrl, hsp, hsto, fun π s2 hlw => ⟨rfl, rfl, fun l hl i hi => ?_⟩⟩
    obtain ⟨hpre, -⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsto
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp
    have hblk := split_block s₁ st.internal (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra))
    rw [hlen] at hblk
    have hlr' : l ∈ cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra) :=
      (cellsOf_prefix st x.base x.size extra).subset hl
    have hlr : l ∈ (splitEff s₁ st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)]).afp
        D.kern.A.length := by simp only [S3.afp, hblk]; exact hlr'
    have hne : l ≠ d := fun he =>
      (hpre.noCover l hlr).1 (by rw [he]; exact mem_footprint_self hpre.usable hpre.leaf)
    obtain ⟨hlP, hlleaf, -⟩ := mem_footprint.1 (hstat.regionIn l hlr')
    rw [hP₁] at hlP hlleaf
    have hdP : d < D.kern.P.length := hP₂ ▸ hpre.usable.lt
    have hdleaf : isLeaf D.kern.P d := hP₂ ▸ hpre.leaf
    have hdis : (π.L l).alloc ≠ (π.L d).alloc ∨
        Machine.RangeDisjoint (π.L l).off (π.L l).len (π.L d).off (π.L d).len := by
      by_cases ha : (π.L l).alloc = (π.L d).alloc
      · exact .inr (hlw.disjoint l d hlP hdP hlleaf hdleaf hne ha)
      · exact .inl ha
    simp only [Refinement.opsOf, Refinement.storeOps, Refinement.writeOps, List.map_cons,
      List.map_nil, Refinement.run, Refinement.opEff]
    exact bytesOf_write_other hdis hi

def Live (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop := s.Active E.internal

/-- Decidability of `Live` (§46). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Decidable (Live s E) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (s.Active _))

/-- Arena value (§46): the place holding `internal`. -/
def arenaValue (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Option Nat :=
  match s.A[E.internal]? with
  | some y => match y.holder with
    | .place v => some v
    | .frame _ => none
  | none => none

/-- `MetaRight(s, arena)` (§36, §77.1, §78.1): exercisable `Modify` over the arena value; there is
no `writeShared` branch. -/
def MetaRight (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop :=
  OptP (arenaValue s E) (fun v => HasRight s .modify v) False

/-- Decidability of `MetaRight` (§36). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Decidable (MetaRight s E) := by
  unfold MetaRight; infer_instance

/-- Available region (§46): each of its leaves belongs to `available`; the empty region is always
available. -/
def Avail (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Prop := ∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ E.available

/-- Decidability of `Avail` (§46). -/
instance (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Decidable (Avail E region) := by
  unfold Avail; infer_instance

instance (s : S3) (h : Holder) : Decidable (LeavesInit s h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold LeavesInit <;> infer_instance

/-- The unified administration guard (§56, §76.4) as a contract predicate: `internal` is absent
from every registry of live administrations. A registry is given by the `internal` identities of
its live administrations; `regs` lists all relevant registries. -/
def Guard56 (regs : List (List Nat)) (i : Nat) : Prop := ∀ R ∈ regs, i ∉ R

/-- Decidability of `Guard56` (§56). -/
instance (regs : List (List Nat)) (i : Nat) : Decidable (Guard56 regs i) := by
  unfold Guard56; infer_instance

/-- The arena registry as a registry of live administrations (§46, §56): the `internal`
identities of its live entries. -/
def liveInternals (s : S3) (arenas : List ArenaEntry) : List Nat :=
  (arenas.filter fun E => decide (s.Active E.internal)).map (·.internal)

/-- Preconditions of `newArena(storage, internal)` other than the guard (§76.1–§76.3, §76.5,
§76.6). §76.6 is read on the resulting state (v0.1 §76.6): its kernel component is `s`, since
`newArena` changes no kernel component (§76 `ok` effect, `newArena_kernel`), so `WF3`, `I1`,
`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are required of the whole kernel state `s`; the new entry is
the one `newArenaEff` registers, `available` holding the leaves of the storage and `issued`
empty, and it must satisfy `ArenaInv` (§55). -/
structure NewArenaBase (s : S3) (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §76.1: `storage` is an existing, usable place. -/
  storageUsable : s.Usable storage
  /-- §76.1: `storage` is under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. -/
  storageRight : HasRight s .modify storage
  /-- §76.2: `internal` exists, is active and has own mode `Modify`. -/
  internalAuth : OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify) False
  /-- §76.2: `ExercisableAt(s, internal, Modify)`. -/
  exercisable : s.ExercisableAt internal .modify
  /-- §76.3: `internal` is held by a place, the arena value. -/
  heldByPlace : OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.holder.isPlace = true) False
  /-- §76.3: `footprint(internal) ⊆ footprint(storage)`. -/
  fpSub : ∀ l ∈ s.afp internal, l ∈ footprint s.P storage
  /-- §76.3: `footprint(storage) ⊆ footprint(internal)`. -/
  fpSup : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, l ∈ s.afp internal
  /-- §76.5: all leaves of the arena value are already `Init`. -/
  valueInit : OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => LeavesInit s y.holder) True
  /-- §76.6: `WF3` (§49) over the whole kernel state of the resulting state. -/
  wf3 : WF3 s
  /-- §76.6: `I1` (§50) over the whole kernel state of the resulting state. -/
  i1 : I1 s
  /-- §76.6: `AnchorOrder` (§44) over the whole kernel state of the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrder : AnchorOrder s
  /-- §76.6: `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44) over the whole kernel state of the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : AnchorOrderHeld s
  /-- §76.6: the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (§55). -/
  arenaInv : ArenaInv s ⟨storage, internal, footprint s.P storage, []⟩

/-- Decidability of `NewArenaBase` (§76). -/
instance (s : S3) (storage internal : Nat) : Decidable (NewArenaBase s storage internal) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Usable storage ∧ HasRight s .modify storage ∧
    OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify) False ∧
    s.ExercisableAt internal .modify ∧
    OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.holder.isPlace = true) False ∧
    (∀ l ∈ s.afp internal, l ∈ footprint s.P storage) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, l ∈ s.afp internal) ∧
    OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => LeavesInit s y.holder) True ∧
    WF3 s ∧ I1 s ∧ AnchorOrder s ∧ AnchorOrderHeld s ∧
  Guarded (NewArenaPre L.kern L.arenas others storage internal) (newArenaEff L storage internal)

/-! ## O18 `issue` (§77) -/

/-- Static preconditions of `issue(arena, region, destination)` (§77.1, §77.2). The static
restrictions of §77.3 are given no list by the text and are not represented. -/
structure IssueStatic (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §77.1: the entry is live; `internal` is active. -/
  live : s.Active E.internal
  /-- §77.1: `MetaRight`, exercisable `Modify` over the arena value (§36). -/
  metaRight : MetaRight s E
  /-- §77.2: `region` belongs to the administered storage. -/
  regionIn : ∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage
  /-- §77.2: `destination` is usable. -/
  dstUsable : s.Usable dst
  /-- §77.2: `destination` is a leaf. -/
  dstLeaf : isLeaf s.P dst
  /-- §77.2: `destination` holds no active authority. -/
  dstFree : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
    OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True
  /-- §77.2: `destination` can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. -/
  dstRight : HasRight s .modify dst
  /-- §77.2: local self-blocking prevention, `destination` is not in `region`. -/
  dstNotIn : dst ∉ region

/-- Decidability of `IssueStatic` (§77). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (IssueStatic s E region dst) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Active E.internal ∧ MetaRight s E ∧
    (∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage) ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
      OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True) ∧
    HasRight s .modify dst ∧ dst ∉ region)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩⟩

/-- §77.5: the effective mode of `internal` permits `Modify` on every leaf of the region. -/
def IssueRight (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ l ∈ region, Allows (effective s E.internal l) .modify

/-- Decidability of `IssueRight` (§77.5). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Decidable (IssueRight s E region) := by
  unfold IssueRight; infer_instance

/-- Kernel part of the effect of `issue` (§77, `ok` effect): a block authority of fresh identity
`|A|`, derived from `internal`, of mode `Modify`, on the region, held by `destination`, which
receives the corresponding anchor; only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`. -/
def issueKEff (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    A := s.A ++ [⟨.modify, some E.internal, region, .place dst, true⟩]
    D := fun q => if q = dst then s.D dst ++ [s.A.length] else s.D q
    I := fun l => if l = dst then .init else s.I l }

/-- Metadata part of the effect of `issue` (§77, `ok` effect; §46): the leaves of the region leave
`available`; the issuance joins `issued` with its authority. -/
def issueMeta (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : ArenaEntry :=
  { E with
    available := E.available.filter fun l => decide (l ∉ region)
    issued := (region, s.A.length) :: E.issued }

/-- Checks of `issue` on the simulated resulting state (§77.3, §77.6). -/
structure IssueArrival (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §77.3: `AnchorOrder` for the new anchor of `destination`, in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrder : EffAnchorOK (issueKEff s E region dst) s.A.length
    ((issueKEff s E region dst).pframe dst)
  /-- §77.6: `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : AnchorOrderHeld (issueKEff s E region dst)
  /-- §77.6, O8.5: `destination` remains under exercisable `Modify` in the resulting state. -/
  keepsDst : HasRight (issueKEff s E region dst) .modify dst

/-- Decidability of `IssueArrival` (§77). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (IssueArrival s E region dst) :=
  decidable_of_iff (EffAnchorOK (issueKEff s E region dst) s.A.length
      ((issueKEff s E region dst).pframe dst) ∧ AnchorOrderHeld (issueKEff s E region dst) ∧
    HasRight (issueKEff s E region dst) .modify dst)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩⟩

/-- Library state after an `ok` issue of entry `i` (§77, `ok` effect). -/
def issueL (L : LState) (i : Nat) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : LState :=
  ⟨issueKEff L.kern E region dst, L.arenas.set i (issueMeta L.kern E region)⟩

/-- The contract of `issue` on entry `i` (§77, §58): `reject` when the entry is missing or a
static precondition fails; `fail`, the state unchanged, when the region is unavailable (§77.4);
`reject` when the effective right (§77.5) or a check on the resulting state (§77.3, §77.6)
fails; `ok` otherwise. -/
inductive IssueC (i : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (L : LState) :
    Outcome3 LState → Prop where
  | noEntry : L.arenas[i]? = none → IssueC i region dst L .reject
  | static {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → ¬ IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      IssueC i region dst L .reject
  | fail {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      ¬ Avail E region → IssueC i region dst L .fail
  | noRight {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      Avail E region → ¬ IssueRight L.kern E region → IssueC i region dst L .reject
  | noArrival {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      Avail E region → IssueRight L.kern E region → ¬ IssueArrival L.kern E region dst →
      IssueC i region dst L .reject
  | ok {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      Avail E region → IssueRight L.kern E region → IssueArrival L.kern E region dst →
      IssueC i region dst L (.ok (issueL L i E region dst))

/-- `issue` as a derived operation (Part XIV, §77): its static checks, then the availability
`fail` (§77.4), then `split` of `internal` on the region (O2) and `store` of the block, of fresh
identity `|A|`, into the destination (O8); the metadata is updated on `ok`. -/
inductive IssueD (k : K) (i : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (L : LState) :
    Outcome3 LState → Prop where
  | noEntry : L.arenas[i]? = none → IssueD k i region dst L .reject
  | static {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → ¬ IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      IssueD k i region dst L .reject
  | fail {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      ¬ Avail E region → IssueD k i region dst L .fail
  | split {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      Avail E region → SplitStep k E.internal [region] L.kern .reject →
      IssueD k i region dst L .reject
  | store {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      Avail E region → SplitStep k E.internal [region] L.kern (.ok s₁) →
      StoreStep L.kern.A.length dst s₁ .reject → IssueD k i region dst L .reject
  | ok {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
      IssueStatic L.kern E region dst → Avail E region →
      SplitStep k E.internal [region] L.kern (.ok s₁) →
      StoreStep L.kern.A.length dst s₁ (.ok s₂) →
      IssueD k i region dst L (.ok ⟨s₂, L.arenas.set i (issueMeta L.kern E region)⟩)

/-! ## O19 `reset` (§78) -/

/-- §78.3 (v0.1): no still-usable place depends on an anchor in the strict origin subtree of
`internal` that covers a leaf of the administered storage. Dependencies of contained values are
covered since parts are places. -/
def ResetNoDeps (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, E.internal ∈ s.ancs x →

content.content:
used per policy ("use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings").

## Readings that change verdicts

**DS-R1 "a cell above m" [draft].** DS-v1: "rejects if an active authority derived from internal
covers a cell above m". Reading: the cells at positions `[m.top, top)` (`above`), those that
`rewind m` returns. Alternative A: any cell at position `≥ m.top`. Alternative B: the regions issued
after `m`. Example (`Witness.reading_above`, decided): after `rewind ⟨0,1,1⟩` (top 1) and the
program's `release(5)`, `derive(4, [3], Modify)` gives authority 8, active, derived from `internal`
4, on cell 3 (position 1 ≥ `m0.top` = 0, but ≥ current top). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `ok` here; under
A it is rejected. Safety is unaffected: the next `push` over cell 3 is rejected by the effective
right (§43, §61.1). Under B, a block grown after `m` from a base below `m` blocks `rewind` on its
lower part too (draft `opsE4`; not re-run here).

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. The explicit identity check changes no verdict
on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft]. This is a reason
to reject that DS-v1 does not list (narrow check ds4-2). Alternative: a mark of a stack that does not
exist is not live, so DS-v1's "fails on a dead or foreign mark" gives `fail`; or DS-v1 is silent.
Example (`../final5/nostack.lean`): on the initial state `d0` (`DReach.init`, no stack),
`rewind(0, ⟨0,0,0⟩)` is `reject` through `RewindStep.noStack` and neither `ok` nor `fail`; `fail` under
the alternative.

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack (`Stack.block` gives none): DS-v1 says nothing. Reading [draft
`case_grow`]: `reject` (`GrowStep.noBlock`). Alternative: `fail`, by analogy with DS-v1 "rewind m
fails on a dead or foreign mark" (an identifier the stack does not record). Example
(`Ern.Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`, decided): after
`grow(0, 6, 1)` replaced block 6 by block 9 (`ds03.stacks` records the blocks `[⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩]`
only), `grow(0, 6, 1)` is `reject` here and `fail` under the alternative (the step reaches
`noBlock` and no other rule).

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

**DS-R7 `push` without room: `fail` [draft].** DS-v1 says only that `push` uses the derived issue.
Reading: the `size` cells at the top must exist (`top + size ≤ |cells|`); otherwise `fail`
(availability, §77.4), checked after `IssueStatic` on the requested cells that exist. Alternative:
"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (3)): `push(0, 3, 4)` on a stack of 2 cells is `fail`.

**DS-R8 `push` static checks are those of the derived issue (`Arena.IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2).**
Not the draft's restricted ones: an `Init` destination is not rejected (spec v0 §77.2, O8.2).
`push` of size 0 is accepted (issue of the empty region): the empty block blocks no `rewind`, and
`rewind` forgets it in the metadata while its authority stays active [draft DS-3].

**DS-R9 `newStack` preconditions: §76.5 applies [draft]** (was R5; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says nothing about creation. Reading: those of `newArena` other than its guard
(`Arena.NewArenaBase`: §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 "All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are
already `Init`", read for a stack) and `Guard56 (stackInternals :: others)` (§56). Alternative: drop
§76.5 for a stack (DS-v1 does not take over `newArena`). Same choice as H-R8 for pools. Example
(`Witness.reading_newStack`, decided on the initial state of statics `wsu`): leaf 0, `Uninit`, owns
the storage leaf 1 and so holds its root authority 1 (§47); `newStack(1, 1)` is `reject` (only
§76.5 fails: every other field of `NewArenaBase` and the guard hold), `ok` under the alternative.

**DS-R10 `mark` requires no right [draft]** (was R6; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1 says nothing about
a right for `mark`. Reading: `ok` on an existing stack, `reject` on a missing one; `mark` changes
library metadata only and creates no right (§36 ¶2, §38). Alternative: §36 ¶1, metadata is modified
"to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts", so `mark` needs a right on the
stack value (`AdminRight`, or a valid `writeShared` over it, §68), else `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_mark`): in `d13` (a callee frame entered after the rewind), the callee has no
`AdminRight`, no `Observe` right on the stack value 0 and no valid `writeShared` over it through any
authority; `mark(0)` is `ok` (a mark appended), `reject` under the alternative.

**DS-R11 `grow` destination: the recorded `Blk.dst` [draft]** (was R7; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says only "grow is in place only" and "uses the derived issue"; it does not name the destination.
Reading: the destination recorded for the block at `push` (`Blk.dst`), even when the block value has
been transferred since and that place is `Moved`. Alternative: the place that currently holds `b`.
Changes the arrival state. Example (`Witness.reading_grow_dst`): after the first push (block 5
stored at place 4), the program's `transfer(4, 5)` (§63) moves authority 5 to place 5 and makes
place 4 `Moved` (`d14`). `grow(0, 5, 1)` is `ok` and stores the new block authority 6 into place 4,
which becomes `Init` (§65), while place 5 keeps the released authority 5 (`d15`). Under the
alternative, the static checks of the derived issue (`IssueStatic`) and `store(6, 5)` are `ok` on
the same released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5.

**DS-R12 reasons for which `rewind` rejects: §36 applies** (B47). DS-v1: "rewind m fails on a
dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m,
otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it". It names one
reason to reject. Reading: §36 applies too (normative: `MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on
the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), so `rewind` rejects without
`AdminRight`. On library-reachable states and for an existing stack, this is the only reason outside
DS-v1's list (`rewind_ok_iff`, R3; that `ok` is then the only outcome is stated by `RewindStep.det` since `b2dcaa9`; before, it
follows from `Guarded.det`, R3). A stack index with no stack gives `reject` for another reason
outside the list, `RewindStep.noStack` (DS-R3). Alternative: DS-v1's list is exhaustive, so
`rewind` is `ok` whenever the mark is live and no such authority covers a cell above it. Example (`Witness.reading_rewind_right`,
decided): `d16` is reached by the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩`, the program's `release(5)` and a callee frame
with no parameter or local. There, mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0 and no active authority
derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2, the cell above it. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` here and
`ok` under the alternative. The kernel sequence cannot realize the alternative: `split` of
`internal` also rejects in `d16`, because `internal` is not exercisable at `Modify` (§61.1).
`AdminRight` has two conjuncts. `d16` tests only `MetaRight` (`internal` is active there); the other
conjunct, `internal` active, is DS-R13.

**DS-R13 a live mark of a dead stack** (narrow check ds4-3). DS-v1: "the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark". It does not speak of a dead stack. §46:
"The arena is **live** if `internal` is active", read for a stack by `AdminRight`. Reading:
`reject` (`RewindStep.static`), forced by the §61.1 check of the derived reset; also by the
`Active internal` conjunct of `AdminRight`. Alternative 1: DS-v1's list is exhaustive (the DS-R12
alternative): `ok`. Alternative 2: a mark of a dead stack is a dead mark: `fail` (under the DS-R2 order the mark is
checked first). Example (`../final5/d17.lean`: `d17_facts`, `d17_only_reject`): `d17` is `d11` (the
rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`) followed by the program's `release(4)` of
`internal` 4. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, no active authority derived from `internal` covers
cell 2, `MetaRight` still holds and `internal` is inactive. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` and nothing

**Q3. §36 ¶2 last sentence and §89 s4 vs HandlePool D.3 (B35).**
- Passages: §36, "These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel". §89, "These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel". D.3, "aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres" and "L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`".
- Readings:
  - (reachability) every kernel state of a library run is in `Reachable`;
  - (step-level) the kernel effect of each library step is that of a `KSeq` of accepted kernel steps from the same state.
- Program: `freeSlot(⟨0, 0, 0⟩)` on `v3`, which the contract accepts. Kernel `endUse` is rejected at slot place 1 and at storage root 0, and the arrival state `k5` is reached by O1–O16 alone (`Lib.HandlePool.Witness.freeSlot_lands_in_reachable`, HandlePool.lean:2216).
  - Under the reachability reading this run conforms (proved).
  - Under the step-level reading conformance is undecided. If no `KSeq` maps `v3.kern` to `k5`, the contract's `ok` violates §36 and `freeSlot` would have to be rejected there.
  - `v3` uses client access to `internal` (Spec 9 caveat, HandlePool.lean:2083-2086). The step-level facts also hold on the run `u7` (`R/recheck3/p1_entry_init.lean`, `P1Alt.alt`), which uses only an entry authority. `Reachable` of the arrival state is shown for `v3` only.

**Q4. HandlePool D.3 exemption vs D.4(3) and D.2 on nested pools (B6, B7; contract, non-normative).**
- Passages: D.3, "hors `internal` et ses ancêtres". D.4(3), "`freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné". D.2, "Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool".
- Repairs listed in `R/reports/fix1-pool.md` HP-1, none chosen. Their scope as corrected by review round 2 (pool-2, pool-4):
  - (a) restrict the exemption to `internal` and the ancestors that are not companions of a live pool or their descendants. This changes only `freeSlot` (`Exempt` is read only by `ContentEndPre`). It does not repair D.2: `ModifyExclusive` stays false, because the `resolve` refutations contain no `freeSlot`.
  - (b) restrict D.4(3) and D.2 to the slot's own pool. This changes no accepted program: the restricted statements are already proved (`pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_same_pool`, `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool`, :1567). D.3's own sentence "aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée" stays false.
  - (c) forbid `newPool` with an `internal` that descends from a live companion. The `newPool` of pool 1 in the refuting runs is then `reject`.
- Program: the entry-route run `e9` (`Witness.e9_reach`). As written, `freeSlot(⟨1, 0, 0⟩)` and `resolve(1, ⟨1, 0, 0⟩, Modify)` are `ok`. Under (a) the `freeSlot` is rejected and the `resolve` is unaffected; under (c) the run stops at pool 1's `newPool`. The records state these effects for `n10` (`R/reports/fix1-pool.md`, `R/review3.txt` pool-2, pool-4). For `e9` they are inferred here from `e9_shape` (entry 7 is an active strict descendant of the live companion 6, covers place 3, and is the origin of `internal` 8) and are not machine-checked.
- Witnesses: `Witness.entry_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false` (:2495), `entry_resolve_modify_exclusive_false` (:2509), `entry_whole_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false` (:2629), `entry_whole_resolve_modify_exclusive_false` (:2644).

**Q5. §89 for stale handles that get `reject` (B34).**
- Passages: §89, "a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure". D.1, "détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle". D.2 orders handle validation "avant toute création d'autorité".
- `pool_resolve_stale_fails` (:1609) proves the defined failure only under `ResolveRight`, the live pool and the legal derivation of the companion. Two cases remain.
- Dead pool. Readings: (a) `reject`: a dead pool's handle is not stale; `HandleOK` holds against the kept registry entry and `ResolveRight` fails. The verdict is the same under either H-R3 order (HP-3). (b) A dead pool's handle is a stale identity, so `fail`.
  - Program: `resolve(0, ⟨0,0,0⟩, Observe)` on `wd`, which is `w4` after `release(3)`. It gives `reject` under (a) and `fail` under (b).
  - Witness: `DeadPool.dead_pool_rejects` (`R/report-check/misc.lean`).
- Live pool with an active `Modify` companion (H-R3, `R/readings/handlepool.md`). Readings: the right is checked before handle validity (`reject`, current) or the handle first (`fail`, which §89 asks for).
  - Program: `Corpus.Lib.H31a` (Corpus/Lib.lean:130), `resolve(0, ⟨0, 1, 7⟩, Modify)` on `h31`, while companion 5 is active. It gives `reject` as the model stands and `fail` under the other order, so §89's "defined failure" is unmet here too.
  - Witness: H31a's conjunct `ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 1, 7⟩ .modify h31.toP .reject`; `R/report-check/refute-o3/live_stale.lean` shows that `internal` is active, the handle is stale, `ResolveRight` fails, and `reject` is the only outcome.

**Q6. §86 s4 (B31).**
- Passage: "Reissuance does not permit reading a former logical value without the required initialization."
- Readings: (R1) a guarantee, which the model contradicts; (R2) a restatement of O9, under which nothing is violated; (R3) add a reset effect that makes recycled leaves `Uninit`, which makes `reset` no longer derived from O1–O16 (Part XIV preamble, brief obligation 3); see `R/reports/arena.md`.
- Program (`Arena.Witness.reissue_reads_former_value`, Arena.lean:2544): issue, write through block 4, `endUse`, `reset`, reissue, then `read` of leaf 1 through block 6. It is `ok` (current); under R3 it would be `reject`.

**Q7. §78.3, second sentence (B32).**
- Passage: "Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract."
- The sentence is false: `Arena.Witness.reset_clause3_not_implied` (:2491), after an issue of the empty region.
- Readings: drop the sentence and keep §78.3 explicit (current model); or treat §78.3 as derived and remove the check. The `reset` of `c4` is `reject` in the first case and `ok` in the second.

**Q8. §47, well-formedness of statics (B36).**
- Passage: "a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter". No acyclicity or order is stated.
- Readings: (a) add acyclic, owner-first statics (the current hypothesis `StaticsOK`, Invariants.lean:141); (b) any declaration.
- Program: statics 0 and 1 owning each other. Under (b), §57 fails at `S3.init` (`R/readings/kernel-defs.md` B#9); under (a) the declaration is excluded. `init_kinv` (Main.lean:580) assumes `StaticsOK`.
- Witness: `R/report-check/records/q8.lean`, `Q8.q8 : ¬ StaticsOK cs ∧ ¬ KInv (S3.init cs)`. Root authority 0 is active and held by the unusable place 1 (§49.8).

**Q9. §51 "linked to a valid origin", with §69.2 (B37).**
- Passage: "Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules."
- Readings: valid means "exists" (current, `Access.I2`) or "active".
- Program W2 (`R/report-check/kd_Readings.lean`:17-26, re-checked at HEAD): `a := derive(root x, [x], Modify)`, `store(a, r)`, `b := derive(a, [x], Observe)`, `endUse(r)`. `endUse` is `ok` and leaves `b` active with an inactive origin. I2 holds under "exists" and fails under "active". The draft's ancestor disjunct of §69.2, dropped by policy, would reject the `endUse`.

**Q10. §61.4 (B38).**
- Passage: "Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations." Note to §61: "without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1".
- Readings: (a) not a precondition (current); (b) a precondition.
- Program: `split` under an unsound `DeclaredDisjoint`. It is `ok` under (a) and `reject` under (b) (`Access.split_unsound_without_DD`, DeriveSplitRelease.lean:762).

**Q11. DataStack readings (contract DS-v1, non-normative; B29, B30).**
- Passages: "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark", "push and grow use the derived issue", "grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise)".
- (a) DS-R7: `push` without room. `fail` (current) or `reject` (§77.2 static). Program `Corpus.DataStack.DS05`.
- (b) DS-R5: `grow` of a `b` that is no block. `reject` (current) or `fail`. Program `Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`.
- (c) DS-R9: §76.5 applies to `newStack`. `Witness.reading_newStack` (DataStack.lean:1314): `reject` here, `ok` without §76.5.
- (d) DS-R10: `mark` needs no right. `Witness.reading_mark` (:1251): `ok` here, `reject` under §36 ¶1.
- (e) DS-R11: the `grow` destination is the recorded `Blk.dst`. `Witness.reading_grow_dst` (:1280): the arrival holder is place 4 here and place 5 under the alternative.
- (f) DS-R2: the dead or foreign mark gives `fail` before §36 (current), or the right is checked first (`reject`). Program: a callee with no right rewinds to a removed mark (`R/readings/datastack.md` DS-R2, `Witness.reading_order`).
- (g) DS-R12 and DS-R13, the reasons for which `rewind` rejects: Q27 and Q28.

**Q12. HandlePool D.3: `freeSlot` of a free slot whose identity and generation match (B21).**
- Passage: "un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité".
- Readings: `fail` (H-R2, current) or `reject`.
- Program: `Corpus.Lib.pool_free_entry_handle` (Lib.lean:313).

**Q13. §71.2 vs §36 (B39).**
- Passages: §71.2, "updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata". §36, "Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage".
- Program: a provider leaf that is `SharedMutable`, with an `Observe` derivative held by the frame and no `Modify`. `alloc` is `ok` under §71.2 (current `AllocStatic.providerRight`, Ops.lean:872) and forbidden under §36.
**Q23. All recorded readings, submitted as the policy requires.**
- `R/readings/kernel-defs.md`: B#1–B#47 and SP-A1–SP-A5. Verdict-changing examples:
  - B#1, §43 one authority over all leaves (∃∀): `split(root S, [[f1],[f2]])` then `pin(S)` is `reject` under ∃∀ and `ok` under ∀∃;
  - B#15, §62.3: W4, `split(a, [[]])` then `release(a)` is `reject` or `ok`;
  - B#28, §69.2 qualifier dropped: W3 (`kd_Readings.lean`:28-34), `endUse` through a `Modify` parameter is `reject` or `ok`;
  - B#33, §70.4 scope;
  - B#45, per-leaf pin flags: `pin(S); pin(f1); unpin(f1); transfer(f1, d)` is `ok` or `reject`;
  - SP-A4, the domain of `StaticPinnedBottom`;
  - B#39, provider usability: its recorded consequence "none on states with `NoDangling`" is false (Q24, B46).
- `R/readings/handlepool.md` H-R1–H-R11 (H-R5 is the scope of the exemption).
- `R/readings/datastack.md` DS-R1–DS-R13, including the missing-stack case of DS-R3 (`RewindStep.noStack`, DataStack.lean:218: `reject` here, `fail` if the mark counts as dead or foreign; `R/final5/nostack.lean`).
- `R/readings/arena.md` A-R766.
- `R/readings/machine.md` S1 (§15.3, "required" bytes) and S2 (byte read vs typed read).
- Also to settle: B44 (definitions of the clauses with no checkable content). B43 (DESIGN.md step function vs §20.1 relations) is a DESIGN.md wording question for its owner, not a spec question (note under the table of section 1).

**Q24. §71.2: existence of the provider (B46; round 0, ops-b F1).**
- Passage: §71.2, "All leaves of the provider are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata". It does not say that the provider is a place.
- Readings: no existence condition (current: the footprint of a non-place is empty, so both conditions hold vacuously); or the draft clause `Usable provider`.
- Program: from `S3.init [((none, none, 0), true)]`, which satisfies `NoDangling`, `alloc` with provider 5. It is `ok` as the model stands and `reject` with `Usable provider`.
- Witness: `R/report-check/records/b39.lean`, `B39.b39`. `R/readings/kernel-defs.md` B#39's "none on states with `NoDangling`" is false.

**Q25. §69.2: is `place` among "the places dying with `place`"? (round 0, ops-b F3).**
- Passage: §69.2 exempts only derivatives held by "the places dying with `place`". The §69 effect says "`place` remains usable as a place".
- Readings: (a) strict literal: an authority held by the surviving `place` blocks `endUse`; (b) `place`, whose value dies, counts among the dying places (current: `Access.EndUseAccessOK`, Ops.lean:709, exempts every authority held within `place`). The mixed reading actually used is recorded in neither `R/readings/kernel-defs.md` B#28 nor B#29.
- Program: `R/report-check/records/V_r0.lean`:54-71, from the statics of `Access.Examples`: `alloc` (provider 0, owner 1) makes place 3; `derive(3, [3], Modify)` gives authority 4; `store(4, 0)`; `transfer(0, 1)`; then `endUse(1)` while authority 4 is held by place 1, which survives. It is `ok` under (b) (`EndUsePre K0 sd 1`) and `reject` under (a) (`EndUseAccessOK sd 1 4 ∧ ¬ StrictAccessOK sd 1 4`).

**Q26. §60.1 "its origin chain and anchors are valid", read through §44 (round 0, ops-a R1; linked to Q9).**
- Passage: §60.1. §44 gives "valid" a meaning: an anchor is valid while the authority it names is active. `R/readings/kernel-defs.md` SP-A5 and the policy record the clause as having no checkable content; round 0 (ops-a R1) found that record misdescribed.
- Readings: valid means "exists" (the clause is then redundant with WF3.5, and omitting it, as the model does, changes nothing) or "active" (as in Q9).
- Program: `R/report-check/records/r60.lean`: after the W2 run of Q9, `derive(3, [0], Observe)`, whose origin 2 is inactive. It is `ok` under "exists" (current, `R60.r60`) and `reject` under "active".

**Q27. DS-v1 `rewind`: does §36 add a reason to reject? (DS-R12; contract DS-v1, non-normative; B47 note in section 1).**
- Passages: DS-v1, "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it". It names one reason to reject. §36, "For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**", and "These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel".
- Readings: (a) §36 applies, so `rewind` also rejects without `AdminRight` (current). On library-reachable states (`DReach`) and for an existing stack, this is the only reason outside DS-v1's list (`Lib.DataStack.rewind_ok_iff`, DataStack.lean:719). That `ok` is then the only outcome is not stated in the module; it follows from `Guarded.det` (`Access.Guarded.det`, MemoryModel/Access/Lemmas.lean:207; scratch proof `R/../records-chk/okonly.lean`, `rewind_only_ok`). (b) DS-v1's list is exhaustive, so `rewind` is `ok` whenever the mark is live and no active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above it.
- Program: `Lib.DataStack.Witness.reading_rewind_right` (:1338), state `d16` (:1329). After the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`, a callee frame with no parameter or local is entered. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, and no active authority derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2, the cell above it. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` under (a) and `ok` under (b). The kernel sequence cannot realize (b) there: `split` of `internal` also rejects, because `internal` is not exercisable at `Modify` (§61.1).
- Scope: existing stacks. A stack index with no stack gives `reject` through `RewindStep.noStack` (DataStack.lean:218), a further reason outside DS-v1's list (DS-R3, `R/final5/nostack.lean`; submitted with Q23).

**Q28. DS-v1 `rewind` on a live mark of a dead stack (DS-R13; contract DS-v1, non-normative; narrow check ds4-3).**
- Passages: DS-v1, "the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark". DS-v1 does not speak of a dead stack. §46, "The arena is **live** if `internal` is active", which `Lib.DataStack.AdminRight` (DataStack.lean:108) reads for a stack. §77.1, "The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active". §61.1, "`source` is active and exercisable by the current frame".
- Readings:
  - (a) `reject` (current; forced by the §61.1 check of the derived reset; also by the `Active internal` conjunct of `AdminRight`, constructor `RewindStep.static`);
  - (b) DS-v1's list is exhaustive (Q27 (b)): `ok`;
  - (c) a mark of a dead stack is a dead mark: `fail` (under the DS-R2 order the mark is checked first).
  - The only alternatives that change the verdict are (c) `fail` and (b) `ok`, and (b) is possible only if `rewind` skips the derived reset. Whether the liveness of the stack is part of the §36 check does not change the verdict.
- Program: `R/final5/d17.lean`, re-elaborated against HEAD. `d17` is `d11` (after the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`) followed by the program's `release(4)` of `internal` 4. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, no active authority derived from `internal` covers cell 2, `MetaRight` still holds and `internal` is inactive (`d17_facts`). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` and nothing else under (a) (`d17_only_reject`), `ok` under (b) and `fail` under (c). The kernel sequence cannot realize (b): in `d17`, `split` of `internal` rejects because `internal` is inactive (§61.1; `SplitPre.active`, the same test as the first conjunct of `AdminRight`). Without that conjunct the outcome stays `reject` through `RewindStep.split` (`R/../records-chk/q28split.lean`, `d17_split_rejects`: `¬ Active`, `¬ SplitPre` and `SplitStep … .reject` on `d17`).
- `d16` of Q27 does not exercise this case: there `internal` is active and only `MetaRight` fails.
